entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is an externally grounded, specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an agent (bearer) and specifies a normative constraint upon that agent from outside — paradigmatically a Role in BFO terms. It is not a Quality (not a mere measurable property), not a Disposition (not internally grounded in the bearer's intrinsic constitution), but rather a socially/legally conferred relation that positions the agent relative to a norm. BFO Role (BFO_0000023) is the correct type: it is externally grounded (by a legal or normative system) and inheres in exactly one bearer. The existing working:LegalObligation class is already typed as BFO_0000023, and AgentObligationBinding could be modeled as a subclass of LegalObligation that specifically emphasizes the binding relation between an agent and the obligatory content.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a species of LegalObligation — it is the subtype specifically characterizing the binding of an obligation to a particular agent bearer, inheriting the Role (BFO_0000023) typing from LegalObligation and adding specificity about the agent-directed character of the binding.

open_questions: Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended as a dyadic relation (between an agent and an obligation-content) or as a unary property inhering in the agent alone? This affects whether it should be modeled as a Role (SDC inhering in the agent) or as a Relation (OWL object property).

Should 'agent-obligation binding' be distinguished from 'LegalObligation' already in the ontology, or is it synonymous? If synonymous, we should reuse working:LegalObligation rather than mint a new class.
Is the obligation binding in question specifically legal, moral, or both? This affects whether AgentObligationBinding should be a subclass of LegalObligation or a sibling class under BFO_0000023.

Is the binding constitutive (the agent becomes the bearer of the obligation through some act or status) or merely causal (the obligation compels certain behavior)? The former favors Role; the latter might favor Disposition (BFO_0000016).
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' denotes the specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an agent and encodes a normative constraint imposed on that agent by an external legal or social system. In BFO 2020 this maps most naturally to Role (BFO_0000023) because roles are externally grounded — they are conferred by context, system, or norm rather than arising from the bearer's own intrinsic constitution (which would be a Disposition). The existing working:LegalObligation class already carries exactly this typing (BFO_0000023), so the new class AgentObligationBinding is proposed as a subclass of LegalObligation, adding the specificity that this is the binding dimension — the attachment of the obligatory content to the particular agent bearer. Several open questions are raised because the exact sense of 'binding' (relational vs. property, legal vs. moral, constitutive vs. causal) could shift the typing toward Disposition (if internally grounded) or even toward an OWL object property rather than a class.
